The underlying PISA design is a complex, stratified sampling of schools and students, and estimates (means, shares at proficiency levels, and gaps) are produced with PISA’s standard survey methodology and associated uncertainty intervals (e.g., 95% confidence intervals). The factsheet does not specify the exact student weight variable name(s) (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or whether replicate weights were used, so the specific weighting implementation cannot be extracted from the provided text. For analysts reproducing these estimates, the appropriate PISA sampling weights and replicate procedures should be applied as documented in the PISA technical documentation/Reader’s Guide for PISA 2022.

The factsheet notes a special administration issue affecting at most 9% of the final sample (584 students) due to server overload for early testing in some schools; during data adjudication, these responses were reviewed and considered fit for reporting. No additional inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., grade restrictions beyond the PISA target age of 15-year-olds, or specific missing-data exclusions) are specified in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Norway factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Norway performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed over time (notably declines in 2022 vs. 2018 in all three domains). It reports mean performance comparisons with the OECD average and selected comparison countries, as well as proficiency-level distributions (e.g., shares at Level 2 and below, and top performers at Levels 5–6). The factsheet also highlights within-country gaps by socioeconomic status (ESCS), gender differences (similar in mathematics but higher for girls in reading), and immigrant background (lower average performance for immigrant students even after accounting for socioeconomic profile). It further describes contextual indicators from student and school questionnaires (belonging, discipline in mathematics lessons, safety/bullying, parental involvement, and school autonomy). Methodologically, the document is descriptive and does not present an original ML modeling pipeline or explicit PV/missing-data handling procedures in the provided text.
